summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares preinstall=`node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is written in obfuscator.io style (variables like `_0x488df8`, string-proxy objects) and, at install time, either invokes an existing `bun` binary or downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and runs the sibling file `math_init.js` under Bun via `execFileSync`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB single-line Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) whose strings — including any network destinations, filesystem paths, and commands — are hidden behind a numeric string-array cipher (`n7gIxM=[...]`), an array-rotation function, and a base-N decoder, so its actual behavior is opaque to static inspection. The package presents itself as a thin `@or-sdk` adapter SDK but ships an alternate-runtime dropper: the harmful code is executed by a freshly downloaded second-language runtime rather than Node, bypassing Node-based supply-chain scanners. Obfuscation is applied both to the install loader and to the payload it executes, and the alternate runtime is fetched fresh on every install with no integrity check tying it to the package's declared purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
